name: Chart Select (CALL Pulse)
summary: A CALL-only rise/fall pulse that runs on a shared Deriv demo account. You can watch every trade, win or lose, on the live board.
rule: Scan selected volatility charts for RSI(14) at or below 38.
Enter a CALL only when RSI turns up and the candle closes green.
Default demo stake is $0.35; $1 only on 1HZ25V 10m.
Markets that drained the demo book are sat out. No PUT book.

risk.perTrade: Fixed small demo stake on every trade.
risk.stop: Each rise/fall contract has a fixed stake, so the most one trade can lose is that stake.
risk.dailyStop: Practice funds only. No real money is traded on this desk.

breakEvenNote: A winning rise/fall contract pays less than the stake it risks, so the break-even win rate sits around 53-56%. Win rate alone says nothing until you compare it with that bar.
limits: The timeframes per market were picked from a 90-day replay. That is in-sample, so the live board is the real test, not the replay.
Demo fills are not real fills. Live results can differ.
A positive demo run does not mean you will make money with real funds.

name: Gold H1 Trend
summary: A simple trend-following Expert Advisor for gold on the H1 chart. It is being built and tested in the open. There are no results yet.
rule: Trade only in the direction of the 200 EMA.
Enter when the 20 EMA crosses the 50 EMA on a closed H1 candle.
Stop-loss at 2x ATR(14). Take-profit at 2x the stop distance.
One position at a time. No martingale, no grid, no averaging down.

risk.perTrade: 1% of account balance risked per trade, sized from the stop distance.
risk.stop: Every trade has a hard stop-loss placed with the order.
risk.dailyStop: No new trades once the day's closed losses reach 3% of balance.

breakEvenNote: With a 2:1 reward-to-risk target the strategy needs to win roughly one trade in three to break even before costs. Spread and slippage on gold push that bar higher.
limits: No backtest or forward-test results have been published. Nothing on this page is a performance claim.
Trend-following strategies lose often in ranging markets. Expect long losing streaks.
Backtests on gold are sensitive to spread, slippage and data quality.
